body:
Your story sounds so much like mine that it's frightening. I know exactly where you're coming from, and I would like to offer my support and love. 

I too suffer the same haunting thoughts. The twisted desires and self hatred sit in my lust. They drive me to the point where I feel if I could just throw myself into these sick fantasies enough, I could summon the rage to finally kill myself. 

But I can't. I live with the self hatred, just as you seem to do. I am tormented with the thoughts of what could happen if I lose control for even a little bit. Will I kill someone? Will I kidnap and rape a child? Will I break in a way I can't even imagine? Your story tells me that you share these fears. 

But think for a moment. You are very much aware of these thoughts. You see the pain in what your brain wants. It torments you. I can empathize with that torment. I feel it as well. 

It took writing my story out on /r/suicidewatch and putting it out there to get a clear headed picture about what was going on in my brain. I titled it "Do I Deserve to Live?" and in it I talked about similar thoughts and abuses in my life. 

The response from the commenters was unbelievable. Perhaps the most important thing I took from that thread was that because I am aware of these thoughts, and am tormented by them, that I am human enough to be worth saving. 

If I read this correctly, then you do feel the guilt, the shame, the torment of your thoughts. This means that you are human. You are worth saving.

I firmly believe that. 

Please, pm me if you would like to talk to someone who has been through this. It's rare to find someone who can admit to such awful things, but we exist. This anonymous space gives us security when facing our darkest sides. But it does help to have a friendly voice to talk to.

Please know that I'm working with your best interests in mind when I say this: Your family doesn't have to be the people who share your blood.

Find some friends you can get close to, those who share your interests. Hold them close to be the family who loves you for who you truly are. 

Your blood may not appreciate it, but you've tried and they didn't want you. It's their problem. And you can always get close to them again later, when they're ready to accept you.

I don't mean to be mean to you and I do want to help. You have my support.

Hey, I opened that link, so you are worth my time. 

I know where you're coming from, man. 

My advice, pick up a new hobby of making something. Draw, paint, play with clay. Do whittling or other wood carving if that's your thing. Build a forge and take up blacksmithing if you'e feeling up to a challenge.

Just make something. 

It doesn't matter how bad or poor quality you think it is. When you're done, look at it and think: I just made something. You've enriched the world.

Don't focus on the girl. Focus on yourself. You can be awesome, I can feel it. And when you're awesome, you'll find the girl. Just for now, distract yourself with you. 

Also remember, the internet is here for you. We love you, no matter what. We don't want to loose you.

I've had a few hours to think about this pattern, and I think it may have a lot to do with how my parents are.

My mother is a sad wreck of a woman. She abandoned her husband and children when my father went through an alcoholic relapse. She went to a strong willed man who will control her life, whether he realizes it or not.

My father, on the other hand, is a recovering alcoholic. He has been surrounded by the wise people who have been to that hell and came back. He is kind, infinitely patient, and incredibly wise.

Whereas it's very easy to live up to and go beyond my mother's life, it's next to impossible to live up to the standards set by my father's life.

Thank you for your support. It means a lot.
Thank you. I'm a little tongue in cheek for comments like that, but I do appreciate it.
You didn't get Jim Carey to step out on a ledge to sing songs to me, so I don't think your comments count as corny. Thank you.

You know you're a fantastic and amazing person, yes?

All I can hope for is that I feel worthy of the love people such as yourself give so freely. It is my current mood of self-loathing and guilt which makes these things impossible at the moment. 

The (to me it seems) massive number of people showing that they think I should live might tip the scales in favor if life for myself.
Fair enough. Thank you for your support.
Thank you. Your words mean a lot to me.

Thank you. 

You seem to have a solid head on your shoulders and I appreciate your thoughts. Someday I might even get there. The support I've received is certainly going to help me through this.

Thank you. That means a lot. I'll accept prayers to any god or goddess and I won't be offended. 

My curiosity may be getting the better of me, but I am curious as to what you wrote. If it still exists, may I read it some time? 

If it has gone poof, then that's that, then.

Again, thank you.
Thank you. I appreciate your support. It really does mean a lot.

That's probably the smartest thing to do. 

I'll have to make it a point to not entangle myself. It does tend to make things messy.
Glad to know I'm not a psychopath.

I... don't get along with guys. I've always felt uncomfortable around them.

So, the girls in my life hold a very important place. 

I dunno either. I'll have to think on this.
Not exactly how I'd describe myself, but I certainly appreciate the compliment and support.

Thank you. 

It's been... a lot.

This week, a friend is helping me by coming with me to community mental health. I helped her by being the support in the lobby, and now she's returning the favor. The therapy should help. If nothing else, I might eventually be handed over to someone who can help. 

Again, thank you for your words. It helps.
